title: Density Correction Calculator
description: Three challenge jobs in which the learner calculates the combined temperature and altitude density correction factor and converts an actual static pressure to the standard-air catalog pressure, followed by free exploration of temperature, elevation, pressure and catalog BHP.
creator: Twin City Fan
subject: density correction factor
temperature correction
altitude correction
standard air
fan performance
rights: Copyright 2026 Twin City Fan. All rights reserved.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
learningObjectives: The learner will calculate the combined density correction factor for a stated air temperature and site elevation, and use it to convert an actual static pressure to the standard-air pressure used for catalog selection, to within ±0.01 on the factor and ±0.05 in. wg on the pressure.

equations: Actual BHP = catalog BHP x Kd
rules: Factors rounded to three decimals, pressures to two
A factor is correct when |answer - model| <= 0.01; a pressure when |answer - model| <= 0.05; two attempts per answer
Job 3 asks for the factor, then the standard-air pressure; it counts as correct only when both parts are
A job-1 factor near 0.35 adds 'Add 460 to each temperature first.'; a job-3 pressure near 2.00 adds the divide-not-multiply reminder
assumptions: Standard air is 0.075 lb/ft³ at 70°F and 29.92 in. Hg (sea level)
Fan at fixed speed: airflow volume (CFM) does not change with density
limitations: Challenge jobs and the 11.0 BHP default are illustrative values
The standard-atmosphere altitude factor is used, not a measured barometer reading

sources: Job 3 and the 11.0 BHP default: Chapter 10 worked example 'A Hot Fan at Altitude'

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Practice with check on each step (commit the factor, then the pressure), then guided exploration
keyQuestions: Why does the catalog pressure grow when the job air is hot or thin?
Which value is divided by Kd and which is multiplied?
commonMisconceptions: The fan moves less CFM in hot or thin air at the same speed
The actual pressure is multiplied by the factor to get the catalog pressure
Temperature in °F can be used directly in the ratio
assessmentOpportunities: Running score shown as 'Challenges correct: n of 3'; mastery is 3 of 3 jobs fully correct on the first attempt.
